behavioral_effects: home.spec uses the isMobile fixture to open the collapsed marketing menu before asserting nav and sign-in visibility, matching the responsive design instead of fighting it
compatibility_impact: None - desktop assertions unchanged; mobile projects now exercise the menu open path, which is closer to what a real mobile user does
follow_up: If firefox flake matters, options are fewer parallel workers locally or firefox-specific retries - both are e2e-config decisions, not app fixes
limitations: Residual: 2 firefox failures that move between different tests on every run, one with a Playwright-internal browser-context crash - nondeterministic browser flake under 5-project parallel load, not a fixed app or spec defect
reason: The marketing nav and sign-in link collapse behind the Open menu button on mobile viewports by design, but home.spec asserts them as always-visible desktop furniture - so four Mobile Chrome and Mobile Safari tests fail against a correctly responsive page
rollback: git revert of the single commit
summary: Make the home e2e specs viewport-aware

validators_run.evidence_ref: home.spec 22/22 on Mobile Chrome, Mobile Safari, chromium
suite moved 10 failed/156 passed to 2 failed/164 passed; the mobile home/nav cluster and the webkit invalid-credentials straggler both cleared
